overview: My career has focused on conducting research to examine the role of physical activity and sport in the lives of people with physical disabilities. I have a strong background in kinesiology, with specific expertise in adapted physical activity and sport. Published in a range of peer-reviewed journal articles and book chapters, my research has encompassed a variety of topics related to the impact of physical activity on health and wellbeing in persons with physical disabilities across the lifespan. Specific areas of interest have included assessment of physical fitness and sport performance, reducing barriers to exercise participation, improving access for underserved communities, and enhancing quality of life. My sport science research has been conducted with partners from around the world, leading to several book chapters and numerous publications, with athlete performance data collected at events such as the Paralympic Games and World Wheelchair Basketball Championship. Our studies have also examined barriers to sport participation for persons with various physical disabilities. Other recent research efforts have focused on active video gaming as a means to provide fun and engaging exercise options for individuals with mobility impairments. Along with my credentials as a sport and exercise scientist, I am a Certified Adapted Physical Educator and Certified Inclusive Fitness Trainer.
